object: 20 litre steel jerrycan: pressed sheet-steel body welded at a central seam, X-pattern stiffening ribs on both faces, triple carry handle, cam-lever spout
understanding: The body is thin pressed steel; the flat faces dish in when hit, but the X ribs and the welded perimeter seam stay stiff and buckle rather than dent.
The handles and spout are thick and rigid relative to the walls; they bend only under heavy crushing.
Hurt by being dropped on corners, thrown into vehicle beds, stacked under weight and run over: corner dents, a crushed side, occasionally a whole face pushed in.
Paint wears through on the ribs, the seam, the handle grips and the bottom edges; rust starts at the seam, the base where it stands in water, and around the spout.
